content: Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 1 (soluble), commonly referred to as PCK1, is an enzyme in humans that is encoded by the PCK1 gene. This enzyme serves as a critical regulatory point in the process of gluconeogenesis, which is the metabolic pathway responsible for generating glucose from non-carbohydrate substrates. The cytosolic form of this enzyme, encoded by the PCK1 gene, facilitates the conversion of oxaloacetate into phosphoenolpyruvate. This reaction requires GTP as a cofactor and results in the release of carbon dioxide and GDP as byproducts. The expression of the PCK1 gene is subject to regulation by various factors, including insulin, glucocorticoids, glucagon, cyclic AMP (cAMP), and dietary influences. Additionally, a mitochondrial isozyme of the protein encoded by this gene has also been identified and characterized.
